claim: When Enterich refuses to start, the unknown-variable warnings are never worked out, so the operator never sees the one line that would point to a misspelled required variable. They see only that the correctly spelled name is "required", although they believe they set it.
evidence:
src/enterich/config.py:load raises before it builds the warnings: `if reader.problems:
        raise ConfigError(reader.problems)

    warnings = [
        f"{PREFIX}{name} is not a known variable and is ignored" for name in reader.unknown()
    ]`. src/enterich/__main__.py:main then logs only `problems=exc.problems` and exits with 2. Reproduced: `config.load({'ENTERICH_CLIENTID': 'x'}, tools.names())` raises a ConfigError whose problems include 'ENTERICH_CLIENT_ID: required' but never mention ENTERICH_CLIENTID. The same variable set beside a valid configuration would have produced 'ENTERICH_CLIENTID is not a known variable and is ignored' in the start line. In other words, the hint exists only in runs where nothing is wrong, and is missing from the run where the typo is the reason for the failure.
proposal: Test (tests/unit/test_config.py or test_main.py): load an otherwise valid environment in which ENTERICH_CLIENT_ID is missing and ENTERICH_CLIENTID is set. Assert that the refusal names both 'ENTERICH_CLIENT_ID: required' and 'ENTERICH_CLIENTID is not a known variable and is ignored'. That could be a problem entry, or a `warnings` attribute on ConfigError that __main__ logs in its error line. Change: build the unknown-variable warnings before the `if reader.problems` check and carry them on ConfigError (or add them to the problems), so main's error line carries them too.

verdict.reproduction:
src/enterich/config.py:141-146: `if reader.problems:
        raise ConfigError(reader.problems)

    warnings = [
        f"{PREFIX}{name} is not a known variable and is ignored" for name in reader.unknown()
    ]`. The unknown-variable warnings are only worked out after the raise, and ConfigError (config.py:96-101) carries only `problems`. src/enterich/__main__.py:18-21: `except ConfigError as exc: ... log.event("error", logging.ERROR, exception="ConfigError", problems=exc.problems); sys.exit(2)`, so the error line has no warnings. Ran `uv run python -c` with `config.load({'ENTERICH_CLIENTID': 'x'}, tools.names())`: the problems mentioning CLIENT are ['ENTERICH_CLIENT_ID: required'], no problem names ENTERICH_CLIENTID, and the exception has only the attribute 'problems'. With a valid configuration the same variable gives 'ENTERICH_CLIENTID is not a known variable and is ignored' in the start line (tests/unit/test_config.py:284, tests/unit/test_main.py:79).
verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading and running the code. REQ-002-PRS-NF005 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:163) says an unknown ENTERICH_ variable SHALL log a warning at start. When the start is refused, load raises at config.py:142, before the warnings are built at config.py:144. Nothing else passes them on: ConfigError holds only problems, and main logs only problems (__main__.py:20). So the one hint that names the misspelled variable is missing from the very run that the typo causes to fail. No earlier check rules this input out, no ADR or backlog entry covers it, and it is not style. A unit test in tests/unit/test_main.py would fail on the code as it is: refuse a start with ENTERICH_CLIENTID set and ENTERICH_CLIENT_ID missing, then expect the warning in the error line. The fix is to build the unknown-variable warnings before the raise, carry them on ConfigError, and log them in main's error line. That stays within the current spec. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: Which journal entries Enterich makes and may change (voucher type Journal Entry, in the company's currency only) is written once as values the create sends and again as separate literals the update checks, so a change to what the create makes would not reach what the update accepts.
evidence: Create, src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:590-595 (create_draft_journal_entry): `saved = await drafts.insert(context, "Journal Entry", {**doc, "voucher_type": "Journal Entry", "multi_currency": 0}, warnings)`. Update, record_to_report.py:603-617 (update_draft_journal_entry): `# Enterich changes only entries of the voucher type it creates.` / `only=({"voucher_type": "Journal Entry"},), kind="a journal entry of voucher type Journal Entry"`, then `if stored.get("multi_currency"): raise Refusal(... "Enterich changes only journal entries in the company's currency.")`. The comment says outright that the update's voucher type is meant to be the create's, and REQ-006-PRS-F005 states it as one rule (create and change drafts of voucher type Journal Entry, change no other). Compare bank_and_cash.py, where the create and the update's `only=[{"payment_type": side.payment_type, "party_type": party_type} for party_type, side in SIDES.items()]` both read the one SIDES table. Example: a maintainer lets the create make Bank Entry drafts (the entry the cheque_no/cheque_date inputs belong to) by changing `"voucher_type"` in the insert body. Nothing ties the update to that value, so every draft the agent just created gets refused on update with "isn't a journal entry of voucher type Journal Entry, the only kind Enterich changes". The same goes for `multi_currency` 0 on create and the multi_currency refusal on update.
proposal: Test: in tests/unit, assert that the voucher_type and multi_currency the create inserts with are the values update_draft_journal_entry's `only` mapping accepts, e.g. by building both from one constant and checking that a draft stored with the create's body passes drafts.editable. Change: define `JOURNAL_KIND = {"voucher_type": "Journal Entry", "multi_currency": 0}` (or VOUCHER_TYPE = "Journal Entry") once in record_to_report.py. Spread it into the insert body, use `only=({"voucher_type": VOUCHER_TYPE},)` and `kind=f"a journal entry of voucher type {VOUCHER_TYPE}"` in the update, and have the multi_currency refusal read from the same constant.

verdict.reproduction: Create, src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:590-595: `saved = await drafts.insert(context, "Journal Entry", {**doc, "voucher_type": "Journal Entry", "multi_currency": 0}, warnings)`. Update, src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:603-617: `# Enterich changes only entries of the voucher type it creates.` ... `only=({"voucher_type": "Journal Entry"},), kind="a journal entry of voucher type Journal Entry"`, then `if stored.get("multi_currency"): raise Refusal(... "Enterich changes only journal entries in the company's currency.")`. The same kind of entry (voucher type Journal Entry, company currency only) is written as literals in both functions with nothing linking them. If a maintainer changed the voucher_type in the insert body, the update would go on accepting only "Journal Entry" and would refuse every draft the create had just made. bank_and_cash.py:539 builds its create body and its update `only=` from the one SIDES table.
verdict.reason: I read record_to_report.py:579-617. The comment at :604 says the update's voucher type is meant to be the one the create makes. REQ-006-PRS-F005 (docs/specs/req-006-*.md:106) states it as one rule: the create makes Journal Entry drafts and the update refuses any other voucher type or a draft with multi_currency set. So the two values are equal on purpose, not by chance, and they are not meant to differ. No ADR chooses the duplication, and docs/backlog/backlog.md lists nothing about it. Both places behave the same today and the spec pins both sides, so no failing test shows a defect. Closing it means restructuring around one shared constant, the way bank_and_cash.py does with its SIDES table at :539. That makes it a proposal, not a fix. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: How a given or cleared tax template goes to ERPNext (its rows looked up when a name is given, the template sent with those rows, a cleared one sent with no rows) is REQ-001's one Drafts rule, but it is written out separately in the sales and the purchase invoice body and in each side's create and update, so a change on one side leaves the other behind.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:264-265 (_invoice_body): `if inputs.taxes_and_charges is not None: doc |= {"taxes_and_charges": inputs.taxes_and_charges, "taxes": taxes or []}`. src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:297-298 (_invoice_body): the same two lines. The lookups are also copied: order_to_cash.py:275-276 (create, `is not None`) and 302-303 (update, truthy: `if inputs.taxes_and_charges: taxes = await drafts.tax_rows(context, SALES.template, ...)`), and procure_to_pay.py:337-338 and 380-381, the same with PURCHASE.template. REQ-001 Operation Conventions, Drafts (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:697) states the rule once for both sides: "a cleared tax template takes its rows with it, though ERPNext may add rows from the items' item tax templates, REQ-001-PRS-F020". drafts.py already holds the other shared parts of these bodies (posted, due_dates, tax_warning) for the same reason. Example: a maintainer changes how a cleared template is sent, say to stop ERPNext adding item-tax-template rows, or to send rows only when the template changes, and edits order_to_cash.py where sales tests fail. update_draft_purchase_invoice keeps the old behaviour and its warnings and result go on following the old rule.
proposal: Test: one parametrized test over both sides (create with a template, update with a template, update with "") asserting the same `taxes_and_charges`/`taxes` body is sent, so a side that differs fails. Change: add `async def taxed(context, template_doctype, given) -> dict[str, Any]` to drafts.py. It returns `{}` for None, `{"taxes_and_charges": "", "taxes": []}` for "", and the name with `await tax_rows(...)` otherwise. Both _invoice_body functions merge its result (create and update pass in what it returns), and the four copied `taxes = await drafts.tax_rows(...)` blocks go away.

verdict.reproduction: Body, sales: src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:264-265 `if inputs.taxes_and_charges is not None: doc |= {"taxes_and_charges": inputs.taxes_and_charges, "taxes": taxes or []}`. Body, purchase: src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:297-298, the same two lines word for word. Lookup on create: order_to_cash.py:274-276 `taxes = None / if inputs.taxes_and_charges is not None: taxes = await drafts.tax_rows(context, SALES.template, inputs.taxes_and_charges)` and procure_to_pay.py:336-338, the same with PURCHASE.template. Lookup on update: order_to_cash.py:301-303 `if inputs.taxes_and_charges: taxes = await drafts.tax_rows(context, SALES.template, ...)` and procure_to_pay.py:379-381, the same with PURCHASE.template. The rule is stated once for both sides in docs/specs/req-001-core.md:697 (Drafts: "a cleared tax template takes its rows with it ... REQ-001-PRS-F020"). drafts.py already holds this rule's other halves (tax_rows at drafts.py:63, tax_warning at drafts.py:314), but not the mapping from given/cleared template to body. Nothing was run: the four places behave the same today.
verdict.reason: I read both _invoice_body functions and the create and update functions on both sides. The lookup and the body mapping for a given template, a cleared one ("") and an omitted one (None) are written out four times: two bodies and two lookup pairs. The only difference is the doctype argument (SALES.template / PURCHASE.template). On create the check is `is not None` and on update it is truthy. That matches on both sides, and on create it makes no difference: Name has min_length=1 (src/enterich/shapes.py:50), so create can never receive "". REQ-001's Drafts convention (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:697) states the rule once for both sides, so it is one rule and not two values that happen to match. A maintainer who changed how a cleared template is sent on one side (for example, to stop ERPNext adding item-tax-template rows) would leave the other side on the old rule. No ADR or backlog item says the sides should differ. All four places behave identically today, so no failing test can show the gap. That makes it a restructure: a shared helper in drafts.py that both bodies use. So the class is proposal, not fix.
